description:
FOUND s492a (Opus, s493 final bar, 2026-09-20) by the probe that member 3
(#1996) had to take: perl decides a bareword in the CLASSNAME slot of `bless`
and `tie` by the ORDINARY bareword rule, so a DECLARED sub of that name is
CALLED there.  PCL always answers the class-name STRING.

PROBED, perl 5.40.3 vs PCL on 268d7e00 AND on the s492a tree (so this is
PRE-EXISTING both ways -- s492a did not cause it and does not fix it):

  package My::Cls; sub TIESCALAR { bless {}, shift } sub FETCH { "F" }
  package main;
  sub My::Cls { "SUBCALLED" }        # a sub whose name IS the class name
  my $h = {}; bless $h, My::Cls; print ref($h), "\n";

    perl: SUBCALLED          (the sub runs; its return value is the class)
    PCL:  My::Cls

  my $s; tie $s, My::Cls;
    perl: dies -- Can't locate object method "TIESCALAR" via package "SUBCALLED"
    PCL:  ties to My::Cls and works

The INVERSE (a sub declared BELOW the statement) agrees: perl reads the string
there too, because perl decides at COMPILE time, and PCL answers the string --
identical.  So the divergence is exactly "a sub of that name is visible ABOVE".

WHY IT IS NOT FIXED HERE: `Pl::ExprToCL::_class_name_bareword` is the s317 /
task #142 rule "a bareword in bless's or tie's 2nd argument is a STRING, never
a call", which exists because three global attempts to read those barewords as
calls broke `Foo::init` in expression position and bareword method invocants
(#142 records them).  s492a member 3 made an UNPLACEABLE QUALIFIED bareword ask
the image (`p-bareword-value`), which reached this slot and broke #142's
invariant that the bareword and the quoted spelling emit the SAME bytes --
Pl/t/parser2-01.t rows 187-193, caught by the gate.  The s493 review fix reads
the marked Word back in `_class_name_bareword` (the site that OWNS the
position), so the slot is a string again.

THE FIX SHAPE, when it is scheduled: the slot's reading is not "always a
string" but "the ordinary bareword rule, decided where the statement is
COMPILED" -- i.e. the #266 classifier's answer, with the string as the `no` /
`not-yet` answer.  The cheap discriminating measurement first: how many bless /
tie call sites in the four populations name a bareword class that is ALSO a
declared sub (expected: zero) -- if it is zero, this is a correctness-only fix
with no row behind it, and it should ride with the next change in that region
rather than on its own.

COST NOTE: making the slot a runtime lookup (`p-bareword-value`) puts a sub
resolution on every bless/tie call, which is why the review fix chose the
string and not the lookup.

Guards that pin today's answer: Pl/t/parser2-01.t (the s317 shape rows) and
Pl/t/bareword-call-01.t row 43 (the runtime half, added s493).
subject: perl CALLS a declared sub named in the CLASSNAME slot of bless/tie; PCL always answers the class-name string (pre-existing, both trees)
